Question Choices: A data set has at least two distinct values. Remove one occurrence of its lowest value and keep all other observations. What happens to the mean?
Hints: The minimum is strictly below the mean when not all values are equal.|Removing a below-mean observation raises the remaining mean.
Solution: In a data set with at least two distinct values, the minimum is below the mean. Removing one occurrence of that minimum raises the mean of the remaining values. If all values were identical, removing one would leave the mean unchanged.

Question Choices: If only the highest value in a data set is increased, what happens to the mean?
Hints: The total sum increases while the number of values stays fixed.|Mean equals total divided by count.
Solution: Increasing one value raises the sum while the count stays fixed. Since mean = sum/count, the mean increases by the added amount divided by the count.

Question Choices: Which measure of center is usually affected more by an extreme outlier: mean or median?
Hints: The mean uses every value in its calculation.|The median depends mainly on order and position.
Solution: The mean uses the numerical size of every value, so an extreme outlier can pull it substantially. The median is based on central positions and is more resistant. Thus the mean is usually affected more.
